subject: Biotechnology
title: Informed Consent in Genetics
description: A short lesson to help you apply Informed Consent in Genetics.

hook.text: Henrietta Lacks' cells revolutionized medicine — but no one asked her permission. HeLa cells raised the consent question.

buildup.text: Informed consent means understanding what a genetic test reveals — including unexpected findings about ancestry or disease.

discovery.text: Broad consent for biobanks lets researchers use samples for future unspecified studies — flexible but ethically debated.

twist.text: A genetic test reveals information about relatives who never consented — your genome implicates your entire family.

climax.text: Dynamic consent platforms let participants update preferences in real time — digital tools modernize consent for genomics.

punchline.text: Ask first, explain fully — informed consent protects people in the genomic age.

quiz.question: Why does genetic testing create unique consent challenges compared to other medical tests?
options: Genetic tests are more painful than other medical procedures
Results reveal information about biological relatives who never consented to being tested
Genetic tests can only be performed in specialized research hospitals
